annotations.title: Compare debt consolidation into a Canadian mortgage

description: Use this when a user asks about rolling other debts into a Canadian mortgage (debt consolidation), for example credit-card, car-loan or existing line-of-credit or HELOC balances, each entered with a fixed monthly payment or as interest-only. Compares three scenarios over a common horizon: keep the mortgage and debts, consolidate at the new minimum payment, and consolidate while keeping the same monthly repayment budget. Shows interest, debt left, fees and limits. Monthly mortgage payments only; 1 to 10 debts. Do not use for a new HELOC, additional cash-out or qualification: none is modeled.

annualCap.description: Annual prepayment limit in CAD. Omitted means the contract has no dollar annual limit; {state:"unknown"} means a limit may exist, so limits are not checked. With a percentage basis, a supplied amount is also checked and the stricter applies; an absolute basis requires this amount.

basis.description: Basis of the annual limit: absolute uses annualCap; original_principal and current_balance use percentage.

perEventCap.description: Per-payment prepayment limit in CAD. Omitted means the contract has no per-payment limit; {state:"unknown"} means a limit may exist, so limits are not checked.

percentage.description: Annual prepayment limit as a percent number in a string: 15% is "15". Used with basis original_principal or current_balance.

resetMonth.description: Month whose first day starts each prepayment year.

startDate.description: Date of period 0; due dates follow the illustrative calendar.

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number in a string, without the % sign: 19.99% is "19.99", never "0.1999".

balance.description: Balance owing on this debt now, in CAD, digits only, for example "8500".

monthlyPayment.description: Set monthly payment of a fixed_monthly debt, in CAD. For an interest_only debt use {state:"unknown"}: the payment modeled is each month's interest.

type.description: fixed_monthly for a debt with a set monthly payment; interest_only for a balance such as a line of credit that pays interest only.

horizonMonths.description: Comparison horizon in months. Defaults to the shortest supplied term, at most 120.

monthlyBudget.description: Total monthly amount the user wants to keep paying after consolidating. Defaults to the current mortgage payment plus the debt payments due in month one.

amortizationMonths.description: Remaining amortization in months, never years: 25 years is 300. Never inferred from the payment.

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number in a string, without the % sign: 4.89% is "4.89", never "0.0489". Wrapped as a fact.

amortizationMonthsAtStart.description: A fact is {state:"known",value,origin:"user"} when the user stated it; {state:"assumed",value,acknowledged:true,reason} only after the user has agreed to the assumption; {state:"unknown"} otherwise. Unknown is never treated as zero.

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number in a string, without the % sign: 19.99% is "19.99", never "0.1999".

convention.description: A fact is {state:"known",value,origin:"user"} when the user stated it; {state:"assumed",value,acknowledged:true,reason} only after the user has agreed to the assumption; {state:"unknown"} otherwise. Unknown is never treated as zero.

fixedPayment.description: Dollar payment per payment period in CAD. Needed only when paymentMode is fixed_payment.

paymentMode.description: How the payment is set. recalculate_payment: the payment is calculated from the rate and amortization; use it for an ordinary mortgage, including a fixed-rate mortgage. fixed_payment: hold the dollar payment given in fixedPayment; it does not mean a fixed interest rate.

convention.description: Compounding convention of the quoted rate: nominal_semiannual or nominal_monthly. The mortgage documents state it. Mark unknown if the user has not said; do not guess.

costs.description: Fees for this offer (legal, discharge, appraisal). A cost the user cannot confirm must be listed with amount {state:"unknown"}; leaving it out means there is no such cost.

amount.description: A fact is {state:"known",value,origin:"user"} when the user stated it; {state:"assumed",value,acknowledged:true,reason} only after the user has agreed to the assumption; {state:"unknown"} otherwise. Unknown is never treated as zero.

atPeriod.description: Payment number, not a month: 0 is the start. With biweekly payments, payment 26 is about month 12.

funding.description: cash: paid out of pocket. financed: added to the mortgage balance, at the start only (atPeriod 0). lender_paid: paid by the lender and not counted.

credits.description: Cashback or other credits, with any clawback.

amount.description: A fact is {state:"known",value,origin:"user"} when the user stated it; {state:"assumed",value,acknowledged:true,reason} only after the user has agreed to the assumption; {state:"unknown"} otherwise. Unknown is never treated as zero.

atPeriod.description: Payment number, not a month: 0 is the start. With biweekly payments, payment 26 is about month 12.

clawback.description: Cashback repayment condition from the lender's agreement. amount: how much of the cashback must be repaid if the mortgage ends early. atPeriod: the payment number that condition refers to (with monthly payments, the month). A known clawback is reported as a warning and is not counted as a cost: the figures assume the mortgage is kept. {state:"unknown"} adds a warning to ask the lender and changes no figure. No clawback: {state:"known",value:{amount:"0",atPeriod:0},origin:"user"}.

destination.description: cash: paid to the borrower. principal: applied to reduce the balance.

fixedPayment.description: Dollar payment per payment period in CAD. Needed only when paymentMode is fixed_payment.

frequency.description: Payment frequency. biweekly is 26 payments a year sized to the stated amortization. accelerated_biweekly is the monthly payment divided by 2, paid 26 times a year, so more is paid each year. weekly and accelerated_weekly are the same idea with 52 payments and division by 4. "Every two weeks" alone does not say which: mark unknown or ask.

paymentMode.description: How the payment is set. recalculate_payment: the payment is calculated from the rate and amortization; use it for an ordinary mortgage, including a fixed-rate mortgage. fixed_payment: hold the dollar payment given in fixedPayment; it does not mean a fixed interest rate.

ratePath.description: Rate changes during the term. Each entry: after payment number atPeriod, the annual rate becomes annualRatePercent (a percent number in a string, for example "5.25").

annualRatePercent.description: Annual interest rate as a percent number in a string, without the % sign: 19.99% is "19.99", never "0.1999".

atPeriod.description: Payment number, not a month: 0 is the start. With biweekly payments, payment 26 is about month 12.

termMonths.description: Term length in months, never years: a 5-year term is 60.

penalty.description: The penalty amount the lender quoted, in CAD. Never estimate it; use {state:"unknown"} if there is no quote.

penaltyFunding.description: cash if paid out of pocket; financed if added to the new mortgage.

monthlyEquivalentReduction.description: Baseline payment minus alternative payment, as monthly equivalents in CAD; positive means the alternative pays less. For the debt consolidation scenario "C: Consolidate same budget" the payment used here is its monthly budget, not its scheduledPayment (which is the required payment). That budget equals the monthlyEquivalent of "B: Consolidate minimum" minus this field in the pair of B and C.

contractLimitsStatus.description: not_checked means not confirmed within supplied limits: limits were absent or incomplete, or a supplied limit was exceeded (see CONTRACT_CAP_EXCEEDED reasons).
